messages:
alex.dev: heads up — we just got a customer escalation (acct ACME) about repeated 504s and timeouts hitting the hosted inference api in us-west-2. they say it started ~10:15 PDT and persisted for ~30m. logs show gateway 504s.

maya.sre: on it. any immediate pattern from the gateway? are these long tail latencies or scale-related 5xx?

chris.ops: quick glance at gateway logs — large flurry of 504s with upstream errors: 'upstream request timed out' and also lots of 'no healthy upstream' around the same interval. Queue length spiked on the request-queue metric at ~10:12.

alex.dev: repro steps from support: they hit endpoint with a bursty traffic pattern (500 qps for ~30s bursts). customer says their retry logic saw 30–40% failures.

samir.platform: I'm checking scaler graphs. KEDA scaledobject for the model consumer had targetThreshold=500 messages, pollInterval=30s, cooldownPeriod=300s. HPA minReplicas=1, maxReplicas=10, CPU target 80%. Looks like KEDA only kicked in after the queue exceeded threshold *and* after the poll interval, so scale-up lag ~30–60s. Combined with model pod warmup, total time exceeded the gateway timeout.

maya.sre: that cooldownPeriod=300s is suspiciously high. If KEDA scales up and then cools down for 5m, it might not react well to bursty patterns.

nora.eng: also saw readiness probes failing for the model container during startup — probe was http GET /health ready with timeoutSeconds: 3 and initialDelaySeconds: 5. Model init (loading weights + kv cache) takes ~25–40s on p3-like nodes. So pods were failing the readiness and not accepting traffic until much later.

chris.ops: container logs show a few restarts: 

```
[2026-03-15T10:13:09Z] model-init: loading weights...
[2026-03-15T10:13:20Z] readiness-probe: timed out after 3s
[2026-03-15T10:13:21Z] kubelet: killing container due to failed probe
[2026-03-15T10:13:22Z] model-init: resumed, warm cache building
```

alex.dev: so a race: KEDA/HPA are slow to add capacity, new pods come up but fail readiness due to too-short probe, then restart, further delaying warm endpoints. That yields 'no healthy upstream' at gateway and gateway-level 504s.

samir.platform: adding that the node provisioning in us-west-2 had a transient shortage — several pods spent time in ContainerCreating waiting for node affinity to be satisfied. Image pull times also spiked for a subset of nodes. Example: two pods spent ~45s in ContainerCreating.

maya.sre: this is compounding: external burst -> KEDA poll interval & high cooldown -> HPA minReplicas=1 -> pod init slow -> readiness failures -> gateway times out.

alex.dev: quick mitigation options?

nora.eng: short-term mitigation we can push in a few minutes: 1) increase HPA minReplicas to 3 for the model consumer deployment in us-west-2, 2) bump readiness initialDelaySeconds to 40 and timeoutSeconds to 10, 3) reduce KEDA coolDownPeriod to 60, 4) lower KEDA pollInterval to 5s for this ScaledObject. That should reduce scale-up lag and stop restarts on startup.

chris.ops: agree. we can patch the ScaledObject and HPA via kubectl. quick commands: 

```
kubectl patch hpa model-consumer -n prod --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":3}}'
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: model-consumer-scaledobject
  namespace: prod
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: model-consumer
  pollingInterval: 5
  cooldownPeriod: 60
  triggers:
  - type: kafka
    metadata:
      topic: inference-requests
      lagThreshold: "200"
EOF
```

samir.platform: I'll queue that change but heads-up: changing minReplicas will incur cost and could affect other AZ capacity. We should coordinate with infra for node pool buffers.

sara.cs: @channel ACME is on a paid plan — they're escalating to account team. We should offer an interim SLA workaround (dedicated pool) while we stabilize. Customer-facing note: explain we're applying mitigations to reduce cold-starts and will follow up with root cause.

alex.dev: let's do the mitigation now. chris and samir, you apply patches. nora, follow up on readiness probe / model init sequence PR for long-term fix (preload on startup or lazy load). maya, monitor gateway and routing for 10–20m after changes.

oncall-bot: incident created — #INC-2026-317 (priority P1) — assigned to /incidents oncall.

chris.ops: patches applied at 10:29. KEDA pollInterval -> 5s, cooldown -> 60s. HPA minReplicas -> 3. Readiness probe updated to initialDelaySeconds: 40.

samir.platform: I'm adding a temporary node buffer pool (2 spare nodes) to the us-west-2 inference nodegroup to reduce scheduling waits.

nora.eng: opened PR to change startup sequence: write a fast /health route that returns 200 once HTTP server is up, and a separate /ready that waits for model & kv cache. Then use readiness with higher delay but allow the router to route small warm probes. Also adding an early async cache-pop step in init. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/model-consumer/pull/482

maya.sre: metrics show queue length dropping and gateway 504s tapering off. 10:36 — 5xx rate down to baseline.

alex.dev: great. next steps: 1) keep HPA minReplicas=3 for 2 hours, 2) revert KEDA cooldown back to sane default after we confirm (maybe 120s?), 3) plan a config change to ScaledObject thresholds for bursty traffic (use 1s poll + shorter cooldown for sub-100ms workloads), 4) engineering to implement pre-warm/reserved pool option for hosted customers.

sara.cs: I'm emailing ACME about the mitigation and offering a dedicated warm pool as a temporary paid fix. I'll attach repro steps and timeline.

chris.ops: repro steps we used internally to reproduce the failure: 
1) run 500 qps burst for 30s to endpoint /v1/generate from a single client (we used locust with 200 workers).
2) clear any warm pods and set minReplicas=1 before test.
3) observe KEDA scale events + readiness probe failures.

Example load command we used: 
```
wrk -t12 -c400 -d30s --latency http://ingress.us-west-2.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

nora.eng: add to postmortem: recommend adding a warm-pool feature and safer defaults: readiness initialDelaySeconds >= model init time, KEDA pollingInterval <= 5s for hot topics, cooldownPeriod <= 120s for bursty workloads. Also consider HPA metrics that include queue length in addition to CPU.

alex.dev: thanks team. I'll draft the incident summary and postmortem. tagging for follow-ups: @nora.eng for startup changes, @samir.platform for node buffer automation, @maya.sre for monitoring alert tuning, @sara.cs for customer comms.

sara.cs: ACME replied — appreciate the quick fix, want timeline for permanent mitigation. I'll include the postmortem link when ready. :thumbsup:

alex.dev: closing thread here, moving discussion to postmortem doc. If 504s reappear ping me directly.
